questions.context: In a classroom in Cúcuta, a chart shows tall, short, young and old people.

options.feedback: Table, chair and board are classroom objects, not descriptions.
Tall, short, young and old all describe how people look or are.
Rice, soup and juice are foods, not descriptions of people.
Dog, cat and fish are animals, not descriptions of people.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta presenta adjetivos básicos para describir personas en inglés. También se conecta cada palabra con retratos del salón cucuteño.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Florencia, a girl says: "My brother is tall and funny. My grandmother is short and kind."

options.feedback: Action words are verbs, not describing words.

options.text: A word that describes a person or thing.
options.feedback: Adjectives like tall and kind describe people and things.
Place words are nouns like city or school, not descriptions.
Numbers count things but do not describe how they are.

questions.explanation: La palabra adjective significa la palabra que describe personas o cosas. También se comprende con el hermano alto y la abuela amable.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Yopal, a boy describes his friend: "He _____ brown eyes and black hair."

options.feedback: "Have" is plural and does not agree with the singular he.
"Has" agrees with the third person singular he.
"Having" needs am, is or are and is not correct alone here.
"Had" is past tense and the description is in the present.

questions.explanation: El verbo has describe características con he, she e it en presente. También se practica describiendo a un amigo llanero.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does Ana like to do?
questions.context: In Mocoa, students read: "My friend Ana is ten years old. She has long hair. She likes to sing vallenato. She is very happy."

options.feedback: The text never mentions soccer in Ana's description.
The text never mentions cooking in Ana's description.
The text never mentions swimming in Ana's description.
The text says Ana likes to sing vallenato.

questions.explanation: Leer retratos exige localizar el gusto mencionado en el texto. También se aplica con una amiga que canta vallenato en Mocoa.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word means the opposite of happy?
questions.context: At home in Apartadó, twins play: "I am happy today. My sister is sad because her kite broke."

options.feedback: Sad is the opposite of happy and describes the sister.
Glad means the same as happy, not the opposite.
Tired means needing rest, not the opposite of happy.
Hungry means needing food, not the opposite of happy.

questions.explanation: Los opuestos como happy y sad describen sentimientos de los niños. También se asocian con juegos de hermanos en Apartadó.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you conclude about Pedro and Lucía?
questions.context: In Leticia, two notes appear: "Pedro is tall, quiet and likes to read" and "Lucía is short, talkative and likes to dance."

options.feedback: Only Pedro is tall and quiet; Lucía is short and talkative.

options.text: They are opposite in size, character and taste.
options.feedback: The notes contrast tall-quiet-reading with short-talkative-dancing.

options.text: Both like exactly the same activity.
options.feedback: Pedro likes reading while Lucía likes dancing.
Both notes clearly describe Pedro and Lucía.

questions.explanation: Analizar retratos permite comparar tamaño, carácter y gustos. También se trabaja el contraste entre dos amigos de Leticia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In San José del Guaviare, a teacher compares: "My mother is a doctor" and "My mother is generous."

options.feedback: Only the second sentence describes personality with generous.
Only the first sentence names her job as a doctor.

options.text: The first names her job, the second describes her personality.
options.feedback: "A doctor" is a profession while "generous" is a quality.

options.text: The first describes personality, the second names her job.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed; job first, then quality.

questions.explanation: La profesión se nombra con a o an y la cualidad con adjetivos. También se distingue el trabajo de la mamá y su generosidad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which description is the best for fifth graders?
questions.context: In Mitú, two family descriptions for a school fair appear: one uses kind words and true facts; the other uses rude words and invented facts.

options.text: The rude description, because jokes hurt less.
options.feedback: Rude words hurt feelings and are wrong at a school fair.

options.text: The kind description with true facts.
options.feedback: Kind words and true facts respect the family and teach well.

options.text: The invented description, because lies are fun.
options.feedback: Invented facts are lies and teach wrong information.

options.text: Both descriptions are equal for children.
options.feedback: The descriptions are very different; only one respects and teaches.

questions.explanation: Evaluar descripciones implica revisar palabras amables y datos verdaderos. También se promueve describir a la familia con respeto y verdad.
questions.subject: ingles
